batch_strategy: Select 32 experiments that resolve specific structure–condition relationships: loading contrasts around recent failures, intermediate points on sparsely measured response curves, and comparisons between related scaffolds with substantially different predicted responses. Use the supplied current predictions as frozen premeasurement predictions. Prioritize discriminating labels over quantile width alone and avoid selecting duplicate condition tuples within the batch.

choices.reason: m125 at 2/1, 50 ul sample and 300 ul DCM is the direct loading-solvent-volume counterpart of cc2a23d8eb9de61d2ab3, measured at 500 ul DCM as 36.23/63.99 mL. Its prediction is 27.72/56.29. This establishes the genuine matched comparison missing from the previous interpretation.

m125 at 2/1, 100 ul sample and 500 ul DCM changes sample amount relative to measured cc2a23d8eb9de61d2ab3 while retaining loading-solvent volume. Together with the selected 50 ul/300 ul row, it separates amount and solvent-volume effects; current predictions are nearly identical across these contrasts.

m211 at 20/1 and 50 ul connects measured 20/1 at 100 ul in bd2e9fee67bbba1155df with the unusual 50/1 loading contrast in 35f2be5f5aa14265e8a4 and 449b809e4efaaf2af86a. The 19.64/43.27 prediction makes this useful for distinguishing loading-dependent curvature from an isolated extreme-condition anomaly.

m207 at 10/1 and 50 ul tests loading transfer against 8f5452ff0e84ab2e2057 at 150 ul, measured as 32.79/61.14. It also forms a fixed-loading 5/1-to-10/1 pair in this batch. The model predicts 30.02/54.01 and almost no loading dependence.

m207 at 5/1 and 50 ul checks whether the early response in ec6846c0fcb7df17c97d at 100 ul, 4.89/10.42, persists at lower loading. Paired with selected 10/1 at the same loading, it tests the sharp ratio response suggested by the measured 10/1 result rather than transferring other alcohols' tails indiscriminately.

m33 at 0/1 and 50 ul tests whether the 18.38 mL finish measured at 150 ul in 003ad1a9637ac1b7c0fd persists at lower loading. The current prediction is 4.85/11.17. This can distinguish loading-related finish broadening from record variation in a common early-onset aromatic-ketone regime.

Introduce seven-membered fused ketone m179 at 10/1 and 100 ul, predicted at 12.43/28.31. Its high similarity to observed structures makes this a test of useful structural transfer. Measured m180 at 2/1 in 983a604ac43bb4d41238 and m63 at 10/1 in c65455de87b41e2ef577 provide neighboring ring-system anchors.

m179 at 50/1 and 100 ul is predicted at 35.83/70.84. Together with its selected 10/1 row, it tests the steep response transferred to this unobserved scaffold. The parallel m180 and m63 selections help determine whether ring size and substitution change onset and finish slopes.

m180 at 50/1 and 100 ul tests a large extrapolation to 42.52/80.96 from the early 1/1 and 2/1 measurements, including 983a604ac43bb4d41238 at 5.96/12.43. It supplies the unsubstituted six-membered-ring reference for the selected m179 and m63 weak-eluent experiments.

m181 at 10/1 and 100 ul fills the gap between measured 5/1 in 8fb7f07df563e78786b2, 11.07/19.36, and 50/1 in 3163a9b58f1a52a1992c, 58.26/97.57. Its 20.62/37.82 prediction is an informative intermediate for locating the lactone's response curvature.

m181 at 20/1 and 100 ul, predicted at 36.80/62.48, forms a fixed-loading ratio contrast with its selected 10/1 row and measured 5/1 anchor 8fb7f07df563e78786b2. This tests whether the previously missed 50/1 tail develops gradually or through a sharper transition.

m63 at 50/1 and 100 ul is predicted at 18.13/38.66, substantially below selected unsubstituted m180 under the same ratio, sample volume and loading solvent. Measured c65455de87b41e2ef577 anchors m63 at 10/1. The comparison tests a strong predicted methyl-substitution effect while retaining the recorded density differences.

Introduce bromobenzodioxole m6 at 5/1 and 100 ul, predicted at 3.43/10.26, as the baseline for its selected 50/1 row. The cyclic acetal environment extends beyond measured bromobenzofuran m8 in bb387f1af7263b2445fb and acetylbenzodioxole m39 in a6a0404c3ad65c6d9326.

m6 at 50/1 and 100 ul is predicted at 9.78/23.61. Its fixed-loading contrast with selected 5/1 tests response transfer for a structurally undercovered oxygen environment. Comparison with selected m8 at 50/1 helps distinguish cyclic-acetal and fused-furan interactions rather than relying on acceptor count.

m8 at 50/1 and 100 ul, predicted at 16.47/32.16, extends the measured 5/1 context in bb387f1af7263b2445fb. It provides a neighboring scaffold comparison to m6 at the same ratio and nominal sample volume, with density retained as a loading covariate.

Introduce dimethoxybromobenzene m122 at 50/1 and 50 ul, predicted at 8.38/22.62. Measured positional relative m108 at the same ratio, sample volume and solvent in dbbaf7572643228cf3aa gives 12.60/20.48. This probes positional oxygen/bromine effects; their different recorded masses remain a comparison limitation.

Introduce para-aminoacetophenone m36 at 1/1 and 50 ul, predicted at 6.26/15.01. It establishes a baseline for the selected 2/1 row. Measured aminoester behavior in 70593725787c65a74951 and pyridyl-ketone behavior in 49201b5817f204116f7f show why nitrogen-containing structures need chemically specific transfer.

m36 at 2/1 and 50 ul forms a clean ratio contrast with its selected 1/1 row, holding density, sample volume, loading solvent and loading-solvent volume fixed. The 7.04/17.39 prediction tests the response of a conjugated amino ketone against the distinct nitrogen environments represented by 70593725787c65a74951 and 064249131c1c3106e540.

m128 at 5/1 and 100 ul, predicted at 15.06/29.22, fills the gap before the measured 10/1 response of 34.88/55.84 in 92f7fe9d8581717a9949. The lower-ratio anchor b655d7de0986cbd0d622 and aldehyde-relative result 4c46ceefd6147b1e0a7a help distinguish carbonyl-specific onset movement.

m31 at 5/1 and 150 ul is predicted at 12.85/28.28. It extends measured 2/1 at the same sample volume in 064249131c1c3106e540, 4.64/17.83, and tests where the nitrile-substituted aromatic ketone leaves the early-onset regime.

m31 at 10/1 and 50 ul is predicted at 30.62/56.14. Measured cyano-benzophenone at 10/1 and 50 ul in c6bd64a77e94e93e5018 gives 17.15/35.53, whereas nitroacetophenone in 9ae9c8b491a04e429a11 gives 28.69/54.81. This discriminates structural transfer among acceptor-rich aromatic ketones.

Compact ketonitrile m47 at 2/1 and 150 ul is predicted at 5.69/9.51. Measured 5/1 at the same loading in 28d8efb10e9abe6740a6 is 15.01/22.58 after substantial historical underprediction. This brackets the response transition in a nonaromatic carbonyl/nitrile environment.

m107 at 2/1 and 50 ul, predicted at 16.25/34.58, provides a lower-ratio counterpart to c6924324ddd95f249df6 at 5/1 with the same loading conditions, measured as 43.20/101.44. It tests how the ether-containing beta-ketoester develops its large response rather than adding another label at its already measured tail.

m94 at 5/1 and 150 ul, predicted at 20.27/43.07, lies between measured 0/1 in d7457b516ddba0143275 and 20/1 in ffffcd6f3b9393846ab4 at the same loading. This tests the onset of the cyclopropyl beta-ketoester's response and its transfer relative to acyclic carbonyl-rich compounds.

m13 at 10/1 and 150 ul extends measured 5/1 at the same loading in 5d530b2f228ed39ff952, 17.85/43.86, toward the predicted 32.92/74.87. It tests whether the established multifunctional-ester curve continues steeply and helps separate its response from the much later m107 5/1 label.

m78 at 50/1 and 50 ul targets an unmeasured weak-eluent beta-ketoester regime, predicted at 28.84/56.22. Its observed strong-eluent anchor aa211a6a6b724470dda8 is early, while ffffcd6f3b9393846ab4 demonstrates that another beta-ketoester can become late. This tests the effect of benzyl substitution and carbonyl topology.

m75 at 50/1 and 50 ul is predicted at 18.91/40.81. Measured m75 at 10/1 and 50 ul in ce3b9d9cbe1699c7eef9 gives 12.68/19.14, while unsubstituted diethyl malonate m80 stays early at 50/1 in 9c10e0827e86bb3c7681. This tests the structure-conditioned response introduced by phenyl substitution.

Cinnamic acid m173 at 5/1, 100 ul and 1500 ul DCM is predicted at 16.90/52.94. Measured 0/1 in 87da8c37b16d810331a2 and 2/1 in 9a32b65bc21fdc5f7286 retain a broad finish with much earlier onset. This tests whether the two heads evolve differently in an acid-containing response curve.

Sterically substituted phenol m58 at 20/1 and 150 ul, predicted at 14.45/25.87, extends the early 10/1 measurement at the same loading in 3ae1262572c1d989fe91 toward the late 50/1 context in 68a01853008546de06a1. It adds a donor environment with a different response boundary from the alcohol families.

m117 at 5/1 and 150 ul is predicted at 21.65/44.69, later than its selected 10/1 counterpart. Together they test a potentially spurious interior response reversal. Measured 0/1 in 25de8af35e546add9783 and 50/1 in d9c8c8af50a10bf07765 bracket the currently unmeasured middle ratios.

m117 at 10/1 and 150 ul holds every recorded loading variable fixed relative to selected 5/1, yet the model predicts a decrease to 18.41/39.21. Increasing PE normally weakens elution as a chemical prior, so these labels discriminate interpolation error from a real local departure without imposing monotonicity as truth.

m120 at 5/1 and 100 ul tests loading transfer from 71abc36775b6cce56da7 at 50 ul, measured as 50.73/71.53. The current prediction is 42.71/68.76. Comparison with the selected m207 curve and measured m119 loading contexts in 776ee2c1e85ebde75168 and e6e78489d1da4066c07e helps separate alcohol topology, ratio and loading effects.

hypotheses.content: Several measured families have steep, structure-specific PE/EA responses, with onset and finish sometimes changing at different rates. Intermediate ratio labels can distinguish smooth curvature from sharper transitions and prevent a global solvent correction from replacing local structure–condition learning.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: The selected interior points supervise response shape where isolated early and late labels otherwise leave considerable freedom for incorrect interpolation. Separate V1 and V2 supervision can improve both onset and finish predictions across related rows.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Do m107, m94, m181, m128, m47 and m207 show gradual changes or localized transitions between their measured regimes, and do both heads follow the same shape?

hypotheses.content: Lower sample loading often delays V1 more than V2 in weak-eluent conditions, but this is an incomplete, family-dependent tendency. Some extreme-condition measurements reverse that onset trend or show large finish changes. Nearly loading-invariant current predictions therefore need targeted contrasts rather than a universal loading rule.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: Matched loading contrasts can teach interactions that the current predictor largely suppresses. The exceptions also limit how strongly loading effects should transfer across structures and warn that record variability may contribute to extreme differences.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Do m207 and m120 follow the onset-dominant loading tendency, and does the m211 low-loading curve at 20/1 help explain its exceptional 50/1 contrast?

hypotheses.content: A large loading-solvent-volume effect for m125 at 2/1 remains unproven. Its late response may persist at both 300 and 500 ul DCM; the previous apparent early comparator belonged to m116. A genuine matched volume contrast and an independent amount contrast are needed.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: This prevents an incorrect cross-molecule comparison from becoming a supposed loading-solvent threshold. The two selected rows identify whether the model should learn a volume interaction, an amount interaction, or primarily the molecule's ratio response.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: At 2/1 and 50 ul sample, how does 300 ul DCM compare with measured 500 ul DCM, and at 500 ul DCM how does increasing the sample to 100 ul affect each head?

hypotheses.content: Similarity and aggregate polarity descriptors do not reliably determine which related structures develop steep retention curves. Carbonyl topology, ring environment, substitution and nitrogen/oxygen functionality may require discriminative graph-level learning even when descriptors or close analogs appear reassuring.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: Related scaffolds with different response classes provide useful positive and negative transfer examples. New m179, m6, m122 and m36 labels, coupled to neighboring structures and condition contrasts, can improve representation learning beyond isolated novelty acquisition.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Are the predicted differences among m179/m180/m63, m6/m8/m122, and the selected nitrile/amino carbonyl environments supported by measurements under their recorded loading conditions?

hypotheses.content: The predicted decrease in both m117 endpoints from 5/1 to 10/1 may be an interpolation artifact. A real local departure from the usual weaker-eluent/later-retention tendency remains possible and has not been measured.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: The fixed-loading pair directly tests response shape rather than treating broad quantiles as calibrated epistemic uncertainty. Either outcome constrains the model's interior solvent-response function for a multifunctional aromatic donor.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: At identical 150 ul sample and 600 ul DCM loading, do V1 and V2 increase, remain similar, or decrease when PE/EA changes from 5/1 to 10/1?

feedback_interpretation: I corrected inherited interpretations using the observed table: 59752d0b8c96b9efb90c is m116, so it does not form a matched m125 loading-solvent-volume comparison with cc2a23d8eb9de61d2ab3. Likewise, c6924324ddd95f249df6 is m107, 71abc36775b6cce56da7 is m120, 49201b5817f204116f7f is m66, and b1c5816f929ef59f5a87 is m106. Their labels remain useful, but the previous prose assigned some evidence to the wrong families. Recent m72 and m114 loading measurements support later onset at lower loading with nearly unchanged finish. The m211 50/1 results provide a substantial counterexample, so I reduced confidence in a transferable directional loading rule. The early m207 5/1 result, together with its measured late 10/1 context, favors testing a local response boundary. The m33 strong-eluent finish of 18.38 mL also weakens any assumption that an early simple ketone necessarily has a short interval. Conflicting same-tuple m72 measurements, heterogeneous m177 endpoints, and the near-zero/reversed m45 interval show that extreme observations cannot by themselves establish deterministic physical thresholds; their causes remain unknown without additional metadata. Historical acquisition errors motivate these questions but are not treated as current-model residuals.
batch_rationale: The batch combines failure repair with tests that can generalize through structural and condition relationships. The m125 design repairs a specific confounded interpretation. The fixed-loading m207 pair, m181 interior points, and m107/m94/m13/m128/m47 extensions constrain response curves with measured early or late anchors. The m211, m120 and m33 selections test loading interactions and their exceptions across different retention regimes. Related fused ketones, beta-ketoesters and aromatic oxygen environments test whether large predicted differences reflect useful graph distinctions or incorrect transfer. The new amino-ketone pair adds an undercovered nitrogen environment at ordinary retention conditions. The m117 pair specifically challenges a nonmonotonic model response. Exact within-molecule contrasts provide the clearest attribution; cross-molecule comparisons retain recorded density and loading differences as limitations. The two m31 rows have different sample volumes and will be interpreted using their corresponding observed comparators rather than as an isolated ratio contrast. Common early-onset and moderate-retention rows are included where they answer concrete questions about finish prediction or structural transfer. These labels should improve overall Row accuracy by constraining both heads across shared chemical families, while avoiding repeated acquisition of already measured extreme endpoints solely because their quantile widths remain large.
